bureau: Credit bureaus licensed by the Bank of Botswana
note: The Credit Information Act, 2021 (Act No. 17 of 2021), in the Bank of Botswana's own copy (read 2026-10-31; the e-laws.botswanalaws.com text is members-only and wasn't used). Section 26(d): a credit bureau shall not include in a credit report any information regarding a debt five years after the final payment of the debt or, if no payment is made, five years after the data subject incurred it. Written as the ZM file reads the same words: a late payment shown five years while unpaid (keep 5; the Act counts from when the debt was incurred, the game from the late payment) and lifting five years after it is paid, 1826 days (five years of 365.25 days). Section 23 has the bureau retain a data subject's information on its database for at least 20 years from final repayment: a minimum archive, not what a report shows, so not used. The Act came into operation on a date the Minister appoints by Order; the Bank's press release of 27 June 2025 says it has licensed TransUnion, Micro-Finance Credit Bureau and Credbase under section 8 of the Act, and the Credit Information Regulations, 2022 (S.I. 101 of 2022, read) were made under it, so the Act is in force; the Order itself wasn't read. Neither the Act nor the Regulations state how many days after its due date a missed payment is reported, so the days are the game's reading: the next monthly update.
